From 1dd8be4ec722ce54e4cace59f3a4ba658111b3ec Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 14:14:03 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] bpf, arm64: Fix off-by-one in check_imm signed range check
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

check_imm(bits, imm) is used in the arm64 BPF JIT to verify that
a branch displacement (in arm64 instruction units) fits into the
signed N-bit immediate field of a B, B.cond or CBZ/CBNZ encoding
before it is handed to the encoder. The macro currently tests for
(imm > 0 && imm >> bits) || (imm < 0 && ~imm >> bits) which admits
values in [-2^N, 2^N) — effectively a signed (N+1)-bit range. A
signed N-bit field only holds [-2^(N-1), 2^(N-1)), so the check
admits one extra bit of range on each side.

In particular, for check_imm19(), values in [2^18, 2^19) slip past
the check but do not fit into the 19-bit signed imm19 field of
B.cond. aarch64_insn_encode_immediate() then masks the raw value
into the 19-bit field, setting bit 18 (the sign bit) and flipping
a forward branch into a backward one. Same class of issue exists
for check_imm26() and the B/BL encoding. Shift by (bits - 1)
instead of bits so the actual signed N-bit range is enforced.

Fixes: e54bcde3d69d ("arm64: eBPF JIT compiler")
Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
Reviewed-by: Puranjay Mohan <puranjay@kernel.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20260415121403.639619-2-daniel@iogearbox.net
Signed-off-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>

diff --git a/arch/arm64/net/bpf_jit_comp.c b/arch/arm64/net/bpf_jit_comp.c
index adf84962d579..4aad9483f8a5 100644
--- a/arch/arm64/net/bpf_jit_comp.c
+++ b/arch/arm64/net/bpf_jit_comp.c
@@ -35,8 +35,8 @@
 #define ARENA_VM_START (MAX_BPF_JIT_REG + 5)
 
 #define check_imm(bits, imm) do {				\
-	if ((((imm) > 0) && ((imm) >> (bits))) ||		\
-	    (((imm) < 0) && (~(imm) >> (bits)))) {		\
+	if ((((imm) > 0) && ((imm) >> ((bits) - 1))) ||		\
+	    (((imm) < 0) && (~(imm) >> ((bits) - 1)))) {	\
 		pr_info("[%2d] imm=%d(0x%x) out of range\n",	\
 			i, imm, imm);				\
 		return -EINVAL;					\
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary

The patch fixes an off-by-one error in the `check_imm` macro used in the arm64 BPF JIT compiler (`arch/arm64/net/bpf_jit_comp.c`). The macro validates that a branch displacement fits into a signed N-bit immediate field before encoding.

### Modifications

- **File: `arch/arm64/net/bpf_jit_comp.c`**  
  Changed the shift amount in the `check_imm(bits, imm)` macro from `bits` to `bits - 1` in both the positive and negative range checks:
  - `(imm > 0) && ((imm) >> (bits))` → `(imm > 0) && ((imm) >> ((bits) - 1))`
  - `(imm < 0) && (~(imm) >> (bits))` → `(imm < 0) && (~(imm) >> ((bits) - 1))`

### Relationship

Only one file is modified. The fix corrects the range check applied to all immediate fields validated by `check_imm` (e.g., `check_imm19()` for B.cond and `check_imm26()` for B/BL). Previously, the macro inadvertently allowed values in `[-2^N, 2^N)` instead of the intended signed N-bit range `[-2^(N-1), 2^(N-1))`, which caused incorrect branch direction when an out‑of‑range displacement was masked into the field. The shift reduction enforces the correct range, preventing such encoding errors.

Here is the root cause:
The `check_imm` macro used a shift of `bits` instead of `bits - 1`, causing the range check to accept values in `[-2^N, 2^N)` instead of the correct signed N-bit range `[-2^(N-1), 2^(N-1))`. This allowed branch displacements that are one bit too large to pass validation, leading to incorrect branch encoding (e.g., forward branches becoming backward) when `aarch64_insn_encode_immediate()` masked the value into the field.

Reason:
The original `check_imm` macro shifts by `bits` instead of `bits - 1`. For a signed N‑bit immediate, the valid range is `[-2^(N-1), 2^(N-1))`. Shifting by `bits` tests values in `[-2^N, 2^N)`, which includes one extra bit on each side. This lets branch displacements that exceed the encoding range (e.g., a 19‑bit signed field with value `2^18` or larger) pass the check, causing `aarch64_insn_encode_immediate()` to misinterpret the sign and produce incorrect branch instructions.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
#define check_imm(bits, imm) do {				\
	if ((((imm) > 0) && ((imm) >> ((bits) - 1))) ||		\
	    (((imm) < 0) && (~(imm) >> ((bits) - 1)))) {	\
```
Reason:
The fix shifts by `(bits) - 1` so that the macro correctly enforces the signed N‑bit range `[-2^(N-1), 2^(N-1))`. For positive values, `imm >> (bits - 1)` is non‑zero only when `imm >= 2^(N-1)`, and for negative values, `~(imm) >> (bits - 1)` is non‑zero only when `imm < -2^(N-1)`. This ensures that only valid branch displacements are accepted, preventing incorrect branch encoding.
